findings.section: 5.2 Proposed Architecture Improvements — 3D stack pin set
findings.issue: Specific npm peer-dependency claims ('@react-three/fiber@9.8.2 peers react >=19 <19.4'; '@react-three/fiber@8.17.10 peers react >=18.0') are the load-bearing feasibility justification for the Path A pin strategy but carry no citable URL and rely on an unnamed-elsewhere research doc (research-3d.md). The libraries are cited in 5.1, but the version-range facts are not independently checkable. Add a citation (e.g. the package's npm versions tab) and mark the pins 'confirm at npm install time'. This is a citation-completeness gap, not a feasibility hole — R3F v8 supporting React 18 is well established and install-time-confirmable.

findings.section: 6.1 New Gameplay Implementation Plan — Location Selection
findings.issue: The report says the location modifier produces a copy of the PlanetProfile and reuses the existing Zod schema, but does not explicitly state the modified profile is re-validated through planet-profile.schema.ts before reaching SimulationEngine. Add one sentence requiring re-validation so the 'all data validated with Zod before use' coding standard is preserved alongside the already-stated purity invariant.

findings.section: 6.2 New Gameplay Implementation Plan — Configurable Mission Duration
findings.issue: The completion ratio (daysRun / missionDurationDays) is said to feed the survival/efficiency component and be re-validated against docs/simulation-model.md, but the integration point (multiplier vs new component) and its interaction with the existing 800/400 thresholds is unspecified. Add one sentence: apply the ratio as a multiplier on the survival/efficiency sub-score (not a new component), keeping 800/400 thresholds absolute, finalized in simulation-model.md with updated mission-scoring unit tests.
